subject: Private enclave evidence index & network narrative request
messages:
From: Dara Liu <dara@verdantmedical.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Verdant Medical Security Team <security@verdantmedical.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: evidence index + redacted network narrative for Private Enclave

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we begin Verdant's procurement review, our security team has a few asks to validate the Private Enclave option:

- A single-page evidence index listing the artifacts you can provide for SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ review (what's trimmed vs available).
- A redacted network topology PDF that shows: tenant egress paths, control plane boundary, KMS/HSM boundary, and public egress guards.
- A short (1–2 page) narrative describing isolation guarantees between Dedicated pools and Private enclaves and where fallbacks occur.
- Any CAIQ spreadsheet you maintain that maps control responses to artifacts.

Can you confirm what you can reasonably deliver within 5 business days, and whether you can do an architecture walkthrough next week (we prefer Tue/Wed morning PT)?

Appreciate it—Dara
Dara Liu
Security Engineering Manager, Verdant Medical
On behalf of Verdant Procurement
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dara Liu <dara@verdantmedical.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: evidence index + redacted network narrative for Private Enclave

Dara — thanks for the clear list. We're able to provide the items you outlined. High-level plan and commitments:

1) Evidence index: a one-page index that lists available artifacts (SOC 2 report excerpt, SIG/CAIQ mappings, network diagrams, configuration snapshots). We'll mark items that require a NDA or formal request.
2) Network topology (redacted): deliver a PDF showing the Private Enclave topology with tenant boundary, KMS boundary, load balancer/egress gates, and control plane separation. Sensitive IPs and internal hostnames will be redacted.
3) Isolation narrative: a concise 1–2 page write-up describing the isolation model for Private vs Dedicated, fallback behavior (model variant routing), and operational controls (auditing, network policies).
4) CAIQ: we'll provide our working CAIQ spreadsheet and a short mapping document showing which artifacts satisfy each question.

Delivery timeline: we can deliver drafts within 5 business days (by Tue 2026-09-07 EOD PT).
Walkthrough: Kimberly and Dev can join an architecture walkthrough — Tue 2026-09-08 09:30–10:15 PT or Wed 2026-09-09 09:30–10:15 PT. Which slot works for your team?

Attachments included for your intake: [Attachment: enclave-network-diagram-v2.pdf (diagram, redacted)] [Attachment: caIQ_responses_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet)] [Attachment: redacted-controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)].

I'll also place source files on a shared Drive folder and send a link in the follow-up.

Thanks—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Verdant Medical Security Team <security@verdantmedical.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dara Liu <dara@verdantmedical.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: evidence index + redacted network narrative for Private Enclave

Laura — quick clarification before you produce the drafts:

- For the network diagram, would it be possible to include a simple callout that indicates where customer data is encrypted at rest vs in transit, and whether any tenant metadata (ids, tags) traverse the control plane? We understand detailed hostnames/IPs will be redacted.
- Can you confirm the KMS scope: is customer-managed KMS an option for Private enclaves, and if so can we see a schematic showing key ownership and rotation boundaries?
- For the CAIQ, please indicate which questions are answered by the SOC 2 report excerpt versus supplemental artifacts.

Also — Verdant's legal has a small redaction checklist they want applied to the diagrams. We'll share that checklist; once applied we can proceed with the architecture walkthrough.

Would Tue 09:30 PT on 2026-09-08 work for an initial 45-minute walkthrough?

Regards,
Verdant Security Team
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Verdant Medical Security Team <security@verdantmedical.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Dara Liu <dara@verdantmedical.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2026 19:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: evidence index + redacted network narrative for Private Enclave

Thanks — all great clarifications. Short answers up front:

- Diagram callout: yes, we'll add clear markers for encryption-in-transit (TLS + mTLS between control plane and compute nodes) and encryption-at-rest (customer dataset volumes encrypted with tenant-specific keys). We'll annotate whether tenant metadata traverses the control plane (minimal metadata only: tenant id and policy tags; no customer PII).
- KMS scope: customer-managed KMS is supported for Private enclaves via bring-your-own-key integration. We'll include a schematic that shows where keys reside, the flow for signing/unwrap operations, and rotation handshake responsibilities.
- CAIQ mapping: the CAIQ spreadsheet will have a column that references the SOC 2 artifact page numbers and a second column for supplemental artifacts (config snapshots, runbook excerpts).

Action items and timeline:
- We will upload draft artifacts to a shared Drive folder by Tue 2026-09-07 17:00 PT: the redacted network PDF, the 1–2 page isolation narrative, and the CAIQ spreadsheet with mapping.
- We confirm Tue 2026-09-08 09:30–10:15 PT for the walkthrough (45 minutes). Meeting invite will follow.

Drive link (restricted): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_redacted_shared_evidence
DocuSign placeholder for any additional NDA/handshake we require: DocuSign: envelope-0x9f3a2b

Kimberly will take the lead on the walkthrough; Dev will prepare the KMS schematic and the redaction-ready diagram. Let us know if you want a pre-read before the meeting.

Best—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
